title: The Last Smile
premise: Sebastian Delacroix takes a teaching post at Hollowmere Academy, where a class of students vanished decades ago and the school's ledgers have been doctored to forget them. Her compulsive documentation — a ritual inherited from her late mother — becomes the only thing the entity behind the missing class cannot erase, and her mirrors begin lagging one second behind reality, showing her what was invited in: a pact made by the school's founders, renewed every generation with a teacher who 'smiles for the children.' As the lag widens into full possession of the house at night, Sebastian discovers the vanished students are not gone but held, smiling forever, and that breaking the pact requires someone to take their place willingly. In the climax she refuses both escape and sacrifice, instead teaching the trapped students to stop smiling — to grieve — which dissolves the invitation; she survives until sunrise, hollowed but free, and burns the ledger that made forgetting possible.
about_author: Quentin Dunmore is the pen name of a former night-shift archivist who spent years cataloguing abandoned school records across rural New England. The Last Smile is his third novel, written entirely between midnight and dawn.

chapters.title: The Position Is Still Open
chapters.summary: Sebastian arrives at Hollowmere Academy on a rain-gray afternoon, interviewing with Headmaster Voss, whose smile never quite reaches his eyes. Her POV establishes her grief-driven habit of writing everything down. Emotional beat: cautious hope masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Room 12 Has No Students
chapters.summary: Given Room 12, Sebastian notices the roster lists eleven students but the desks sit empty. A janitor, Mrs. Okonkwo, warns her not to correct the register. POV Sebastian. Beat: first unease, the sense of rules no one will explain.

chapters.title: Documentation Is a Kind of Prayer
chapters.summary: A flashback-tinged chapter in Sebastian's POV unpacking her mother's death and the notebooks she keeps to hold reality together. She begins a dedicated ledger for Hollowmere. Beat: tenderness and compulsion intertwined.

chapters.title: The Class Photo That Isn't There
chapters.summary: In the archive, Sebastian finds a 1974 yearbook with one class photo razored out and the page renumbered. Voss catches her and offers a warm, rehearsed explanation. POV Sebastian. Beat: the first confirmed lie.

chapters.title: Eleven Names
chapters.summary: Sebastian reconstructs eleven names from marginalia and attendance slips, including a girl called Wren Halloway. At night she hears faint recitation through the walls. POV Sebastian. Beat: obsession kindling.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: Her bathroom mirror reflects her raising a hand one second after she does it. She tests it with matches, clocks, a second mirror — all lagging now. POV Sebastian. Beat: dread crystallizing into certainty.

chapters.title: Smile for the Children
chapters.summary: Voss asks her to chaperone an evening 'reception' for alumni, repeating the phrase 'smile for the children' like a password. She declines; that night the lag stretches to three seconds. POV Sebastian. Beat: pressure applied politely.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: In the lagging mirror, Sebastian sees a small figure standing behind her reflection — a girl in a 1970s uniform, smiling too widely. When Sebastian turns, no one is there. POV Sebastian. Beat: terror with a human face.

chapters.title: Mrs. Okonkwo's Confession
chapters.summary: POV shift to Mrs. Okonkwo, who has cleaned Hollowmere for forty years. She reveals teachers are chosen, not hired, and that her sister was among the eleven. Beat: guilt, warning, the cost of silence.

chapters.title: The Founder's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sebastian finds the founders' original ledger: a covenant binding 'one smile per generation' to keep something fed beneath the school. Her own name is already inked in fresh handwriting. POV Sebastian. Beat: horror of predestination.

chapters.title: What Was Invited In
chapters.summary: Through the widening mirror-lag, Sebastian witnesses the reception she refused: staff seated before empty chairs, speaking to absent students, faces slack with joy. POV Sebastian. Beat: understanding the machinery of belonging weaponized.

chapters.title: The House Holds Its Breath
chapters.summary: Doors in her cottage rearrange overnight; the lag reaches five seconds. She anchors herself by reading her mother's letters aloud. POV Sebastian. Beat: defiance through ritual.

chapters.title: Attendance
chapters.summary: Morning roll call: eleven students appear in her classroom, real as daylight, answering to the old names. Colleagues see nothing wrong. Only Sebastian's ledger records them as impossible. POV Sebastian. Beat: uncanny warmth — she wants to belong to them.

chapters.title: Wren's Essay
chapters.summary: Wren Halloway submits an essay dated 1974 describing 'the smiling game' the founders taught. Sebastian realizes the students don't know they're dead. POV Sebastian. Beat: heartbreak sharpening resolve.

chapters.title: Voss's Version
chapters.summary: POV Voss: he was nearly taken thirty years ago and survived by cooperating. He believes the pact is mercy — better smiling than grieving. Beat: antagonist made sympathetic; duty versus love framed.

chapters.title: The Second Behind the Wall
chapters.summary: Sebastian steps through the mirror during its lag and finds the 'second' itself: a frozen corridor where the eleven wait, smiling, time pooling like water. POV Sebastian. Beat: awe and violation.

chapters.title: Rules of the Lag
chapters.summary: Mrs. Okonkwo shares survival lore: never smile back, never accept a gift, never say goodbye. Sebastian writes the rules into her ledger and feels the book grow warm. POV Sebastian. Beat: fragile armor.

chapters.title: A Gift Left on Her Desk
chapters.summary: Someone leaves Wren's hair ribbon on Sebastian's desk — a gift. She nearly thanks the air before catching herself. The lag stutters, offended. POV Sebastian. Beat: near-fatal kindness.

chapters.title: The Other New Teacher
chapters.summary: Sebastian finds records of predecessors: a 1998 teacher whose notebook ends mid-sentence, a 2011 teacher listed as 'resigned.' Their belongings sit boxed in the attic, smiles in every photograph. POV Sebastian. Beat: lineage of the lost.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Voss, softening, admits he loved one of the eleven and has kept the pact running hoping to see her again. He begs Sebastian to renew it willingly. POV alternates via a recorded conversation. Beat: the theme made explicit.

chapters.title: Midterm of the Smiling Game
chapters.summary: The eleven students take a test only Sebastian can see, answers written in 1974 handwriting appearing in her ledger. Wren writes: 'We are tired of smiling.' POV Sebastian. Beat: hope — they can be reached.

chapters.title: The Lag Becomes a Door
chapters.summary: The mirror-lag hits ten seconds; the cottage at night is fully the other place. Sebastian survives till dawn by staying inside chalk circles copied from the founders' ledger margins. POV Sebastian. Beat: siege mentality.

chapters.title: Okonkwo's Price
chapters.summary: Mrs. Okonkwo tries to burn the founders' ledger and is caught mid-smile by whatever watches from the walls. Sebastian saves her by tearing out the page bearing her name. POV alternating. Beat: love against duty, paid forward.

chapters.title: What the School Feeds On
chapters.summary: Research montage in Sebastian's POV: the entity is not a demon but a hunger for unearned joy — belonging without grief. The founders fed it children's forced happiness. Beat: thematic revelation.

chapters.title: Sunrise Interview
chapters.summary: Voss formally asks Sebastian to sign the renewal at Friday's centennial reception. Refusal means dismissal; signing means joining the eleven. POV Sebastian. Beat: the trap closes with courtesy.

chapters.title: Wren in Daylight
chapters.summary: Wren appears outside the mirror's reach, aging visibly, and tells Sebastian the truth: they were never invited guests — they were the meal. She asks to be forgotten properly, not saved. POV Sebastian. Beat: devastating clarity.

chapters.title: The Plan Written in Pencil
chapters.summary: Sebastian drafts her plan in pencil so it can be erased even from fate: teach the eleven to grieve, break the smile, let the invitation lapse at sunrise. POV Sebastian. Beat: resolve replacing fear.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Through the lag, Sebastian holds an illicit class in the frozen corridor: memory exercises, naming the dead, permission to cry. One by one, smiles crack. POV Sebastian. Beat: found family forming in the wrong side of time.

chapters.title: Voss Learns the Truth
chapters.summary: Sebastian shows Voss his beloved student's face mid-grief — alive with sorrow rather than hollow joy. He shatters, then chooses to help, unlocking the centennial hall. POV Voss. Beat: antagonist redeemed at cost.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: The entity retaliates: every mirror in town lags, Okonkwo disappears, Sebastian's ledgers begin rewriting themselves. She copies everything by hand into her mother's last notebook. POV Sebastian. Beat: darkest hour, faith tested.

chapters.title: Centennial Reception
chapters.summary: The whole town attends the reception; eleven empty chairs face the crowd. Voss introduces Sebastian as the next to 'smile for the children.' She walks to the front carrying her ledger like a shield. POV Sebastian. Beat: calm before the climax.

chapters.title: The Smile They Want
chapters.summary: The entity wears the assembled faces of the missing, offering Sebastian perfect belonging — her mother's voice, Wren's friendship, a family that never leaves. She almost says yes. POV Sebastian. Beat: temptation at maximum.

chapters.title: Grief Lesson
chapters.summary: Climax part one: Sebastian teaches publicly, aloud, the names of the eleven and how they died, forcing the room to mourn instead of smile. The entity convulses; mirrors shatter outward. POV Sebastian. Beat: truth as exorcism.

chapters.title: Wren Stops Smiling
chapters.summary: Climax part two: Wren, at the front of the frozen corridor, lets her face fall and weeps for the first time in fifty years. The other ten follow. The invitation, built on joy, collapses. POV shifts briefly to Wren. Beat: liberation through sorrow.

chapters.title: The Empty Chair
chapters.summary: The entity, starving, offers Sebastian the seat herself — one willing smile could sustain it another century. With Voss and the grieving eleven watching, she sits down in the chair and does not smile. POV Sebastian. Beat: refusal as victory.

chapters.title: Sunrise
chapters.summary: Dawn floods the hall; the lag snaps shut; the mirrors reflect in real time for the first time since her arrival. The eleven fade — not taken, but released — Wren last, unsmiling and at peace. POV Sebastian. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Ink
chapters.summary: Sebastian burns the founders' ledger and files her own final report: eleven names restored to the record, cause of closure documented. Voss resigns; Okonkwo returns, older and lighter. POV Sebastian. Beat: accounting, at last honest.

chapters.title: The Classroom Without Them
chapters.summary: Sebastian stays to finish the term, teaching actual living students in Room 12. Grief and gratitude coexist; she cries freely for the first time since her mother died. POV Sebastian. Beat: healing without forgetting.

chapters.title: What the Mirror Keeps
chapters.summary: One mirror in her cottage still lags — half a second now. Sometimes Wren's outline passes through it, not trapped, just passing. Sebastian waves; the reflection waves back on time. POV Sebastian. Beat: bittersweet haunting, love outlasting duty.

chapters.title: The Last Smile
chapters.summary: Final chapter: Sebastian donates her complete Hollowmere archive to the county library under glass, titled 'So No One Is Forgotten.' On the last page of her last notebook she writes a single sentence and, finally, allows herself one small, true smile. POV Sebastian. Beat: peace earned, story sealed.
